What Are Hydrocarbons?

Hydrocarbons are organic compounds made up of carbon and hydrogen atoms only, making them the simplest form of organic substance. Because a carbon atom can bond with up to four other atoms, hydrocarbons can form an astonishing diversity of molecules, from the methane in natural gas to the long chains inside crude oil. They are the raw material of fuels and petrochemicals, and the foundation of the modern energy economy.

  • Made of carbon and hydrogen atoms only
  • Carbon can bond with up to four other atoms
  • The simplest form of organic compound
  • The raw material of fuels and petrochemicals

Three Families: Alkanes, Alkenes, Alkynes

Hydrocarbons are grouped into homologous series based on the type of bond between their carbon atoms. Alkanes are saturated, with only single bonds (CnH2n+2), and are the most stable and least reactive. Alkenes carry at least one double bond (CnH2n) and alkynes at least one triple bond (CnH2n-2), which makes both families unsaturated and more reactive.

Timeline

A Long History of Oil

Humans have used hydrocarbons for thousands of years, long before the modern oil industry. From Mesopotamian adhesives to the gushers that launched the modern petroleum age, the story of hydrocarbons is the story of energy itself.

  1. 3000 BCMesopotamians used rock oil in architectural adhesives, ship caulks, medicines, and roads
  2. 2000 BCThe Chinese refined crude oil for lighting and heating
  3. 600 ADArab and Persian chemists found petroleum's lighter elements could be mixed with quicklime
  4. 1858First oil well in North America at Oil Springs, Ontario, Canada
  5. 1859Colonel Drake's discovery well at Titusville, Pennsylvania
  6. 1860First commercial oil production in Romania
  7. 1901The Spindletop gusher erupted near Beaumont, Texas
  8. 2009The US became the world's top natural gas producer

The Global Oil Market

Global oil production in January 2026 averaged 84.5 million barrels per day, with the ten largest producing countries accounting for about 73 percent of the total. The United States produced 13.2 million barrels per day that month, remaining the world's top producer, while OPEC+ countries accounted for roughly 55 percent of global crude oil production. The GCC states alone supply 22 percent of the world's oil, and the greater Gulf region including Iraq and Iran produces 31 percent.

  • 84.5 million barrels per day of global oil production (January 2026)
  • Top ten countries produce about 73 percent of the total
  • OPEC+ accounts for about 55 percent of global crude oil
  • The US produced 13.2 million barrels per day in January 2026

From the Well to Your Life

Hydrocarbons are everywhere in daily life. Crude oil is refined into gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel, while natural gas heats homes and generates electricity. Petrochemicals made from hydrocarbons become plastics, fertilizers, medicines, and synthetic fibers. Since 2008, US petroleum and natural gas production has increased by nearly 60 percent, driven by the shale boom, and US liquefied natural gas exports quadrupled between 2016 and 2017.

  • Refined into gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel
  • Petrochemicals become plastics, fertilizers, and medicines
  • US production up nearly 60 percent since 2008
  • US LNG exports quadrupled from 2016 to 2017
